open_points.subject: Model M12 — StoreHistory
open_points.text: A restored store therefore holds this record exactly as the backup holds it — the backup's last sequence number, and its migration closure when the backup was made after the import, none when it was made before — and Registry neither knows nor records that the store was restored.
open_points.question: When a backup replaces a lost store, is the StoreHistory entity from the backup continued as the same entity, or is a new StoreHistory entity minted from the backup's facts; if it is new, who mints it?
options: The restored store continues the same StoreHistory entity captured in the backup.
The owner or disaster-recovery boundary mints a new StoreHistory entity from the backup's facts.
Registry mints a new StoreHistory when it first opens the restored store.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restored store as having a new StoreHistory entity, minted by the disaster-recovery boundary from the backup's facts, because identity is defined by the store that holds it and R0-89 gives the restored store its own history.

open_points.subject: Model M12 — StoreHistory reads
open_points.text: No caller reads it as such: the audit view, the backup record (A18) and the import's refusal (R0-79) read its facts.
open_points.question: Which StoreHistory fact does each named product action read, and does “read” mean that the fact is returned to the caller or only used internally?
options: The audit view reads the last sequence number, the import refusal reads the migration closure, and the backup reads both; none exposes StoreHistory as a model.
Each of the audit view, backup record and import refusal reads both facts internally.
One or more of the actions returns one or both StoreHistory facts in its product answer.
open_points.default_guess: The audit view reads only the last sequence number, the import refusal reads only the migration closure, and the backup reads both; the facts are internal except where the later action contract explicitly includes their values.

open_points.subject: Model M12 — StoreHistory
open_points.text:
The two facts change for different reasons — every audit append, and the
one import — but they are kept in one record because they share one scope
and one life, the store's history (R0-89), and no caller reads either apart
from the store it is in. Each is changed only by its own transaction, and
neither changes the other.
open_points.rule: Не смешивай таблицы только потому, что у них похожая форма. Решение о merge/split принимается по change-axis: что меняется вместе и по одной причине.
open_points.question: The passage must split the independently changing audit-sequence and migration-closure facts into models aligned with their separate change axes, or replace this rationale with one showing that the facts change together and for one reason.
